Comment les escrocs prennent-ils le contrôle des comptes WhatsApp ? Pourquoi est-il parfois si difficile de les récupérer ? Et Meta protège-t-il suffisamment ses utilisateurs africains ?

Dans le Focus du samedi du Journal de l'Afrique, Fatimata Wane reçoit Qemal Affagnon, coordinateur régional pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest au sein de l'organisation Internet Sans Frontières.

The prime minister has defined and dominated his country’s politics for three decades and is putting his rivals on the defensive before Tuesday’s general election

They chant his name, they cheer and clap – and yet he is not the most dominant person in the room. Looming over the crowd that has gathered to hear Gadi Eisenkot, the former general who is the lead opposition challenger in Tuesday’s Israeli election, is a man who is not there. It is the man Eisenkot seeks to replace as prime minister, the man who first served in that role three decades ago and who has held it, on and off, for 19 of the past 30 years. It is Benjamin Netanyahu.

Naturally, the warm-up speakers at this evening rally in the modest city of Modi’in, halfway between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, stress the virtues of Eisenkot, a son of working-class Moroccan Jews who rose through the ranks to become chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and entered politics only four years ago.
